title: pr_merge: retire the merge-time fix cap; enumerate owner-gated controls

labels.name: infrastructure
labels.description: Foundational definitions, shared APIs, or supporting layers

body:
<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: pr-merge-retire-the-merge-time-fix-cap-3279d293 -->
Merge gate 6 in `local/bin/pr_merge.py` refuses a PR whose `[codex-auto-fix]`/`[codex-review-fix]` commit count since the merge base exceeds `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP` (default 5), telling the operator the PR "needs human attention". On 2026-09-02 this blocked PR #5 (six hand-authored review-fix commits, every CI context green, review APPROVED with zero unresolved findings) and the operator escalated to the owner.

The count is redundant: gates 3/4 already require all CI contexts and the review to be green on the exact head SHA, and `autofix.sh` reads the same env var to bound its own loop, so the merge-time count was never an independent bound. Its only effect is to demand owner action on a green PR.

Change (one commit, well under the 400-line budget):
1. `pr_merge.py`: drop the count refusal and the `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP` read; keep the fix-lock probe and the merge-base computation that gate 7 reuses; print the count for the record.
2. `autofix.sh` cap note and `autofix.md` §5: "operator review required" wording; the doc matches the code (the label is not removed).
3. `.githooks/pre-commit`: the scope-control budget runs before the `MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS` exit, so a blanket hook skip cannot launder the owner-only override.
4. `issues-prs.md` §3/§5, `review.md` merge-gate paragraph, `meta.md` §1, `personas/main.md`: exactly one owner-gated control (`MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE`); the operator adjudicates; an owner-blocked item becomes a `needs-owner` issue and the session continues.
5. Worker personas: repair commits use plain `fix(...)` subjects; the `[codex-*-fix]` prefixes are reserved for `autofix.sh`.
6. `EVOLUTION.md` entry; the `events.md` disposition is recorded by the operator with its pending telemetry commit.

<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: stage-42-residual -->
### Precise mathematical statement

Create the full Stage 4.2 Lean skeleton for every QPBT blueprint node in chapters
11--13 that is outside the Stage 4.1 closure. Every mathematical definition must have
a real body; proposition-valued proof obligations may use the tracked Stage 4.2
`sorry` policy. Preserve the source statements and the canonical fixed-field model.

### Mathematical source

- Primary paper mirrors: `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex`,
  `05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex`, `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex`,
  `07_types.tex`, and `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex`.
- Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex` through
  `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`.
- Binding implementation contract:
  `local/briefs/42-residual-brief.md`, including its 2026-09-02 operator adjudication.

### Target Lean declarations

Add the residual algebra, game-calculus, low-degree, Magic Square, completeness,
qubit-form, and canonical-parameter modules listed in the brief. The residual wave owns
the canonical-model decoding/binary-representation views, `SymmetricGame`, and the
shared error/distribution leaf infrastructure. It also owns `Strategy.IsProjective`,
state-dependent consistency, the original `linePointDist`, `opDistSq`, and the neutral
state helpers relocated from `Test/Soundness.lean`, plus `vecTensor` and `prodShuffle`.
It owns the generic `Fintype`
instance for bounded `polyFunc`, which is required by `PolyMeas` and later consumed by
ch15; the existing subtype `DecidableEq` is reused.

### Mathematical dependencies

- PR #5 must merge before implementation begins.
- Tracking issue #1.
- Existing paper-gap notes for symmetrization and LDT dimension divisibility.

### Implementation constraints

- Remove all stale `FieldModel` assumptions; use `P.model` and `L.model`.
- Move `conjIsometry`, `reindexState`, and `isometryTensor` to the neutral
  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/State.lean` leaf; no residual module may import `Test/Soundness.lean`.
  Generalize `isometryTensor` to arbitrary finite codomain index types, and define real
  `vecTensor` and `prodShuffle` helpers in the same leaf.
- Do not introduce `SelfDualNormalRep` or another basis/model input.
- Keep decoding, basis-coordinate, trace/dot-product, and Magic Square
  anticommutation source nodes generic; add canonical `FixedFieldModel`
  specializations for QPBT consumers.
- Implement the tagged canonical `LineDesc`, the source-general `PolyMeasFamily`, and
  the transported common-index `AreCloseStrategies` contract from the adjudication.
- State the unrestricted twisted-commutation and cancellation nodes over a general prime
  with `MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffChar`. Keep characteristic-two QPBT results as
  separately named specializations and never link them as the source theorems. Create
  `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_characteristic-two-pauli-scope.tex` and cite it from the scoped
  consumer declarations.
- Define `PolyMeas` over the actual bounded `polyFunc` subtype. Provide a generic
  `Fintype` instance with the existing `Module.finite_of_finite` and
  `Fintype.ofFinite` route; reuse the existing subtype `DecidableEq`. No coefficient
  equivalence or competing equality instance is needed. Declare dependent aliases
  noncomputable.
- Keep `deltaLd` distinct from `deltaQld`.
- Give the close-strategy value theorem the source's separate transported state-equality
  hypothesis; general strategy closeness alone is insufficient.
- Quantify the constants in Magic Square rigidity and close-strategy value stability
  before all strategies and error parameters. Do the same for commutation analysis and
  the low-degree sandwich bound. Preserve the `0 ≤ ε` boundary in the qubit soundness
  corollary, use `P.model.basisDim`, and add no field-model or basis argument.
- Serialize the aggregate `MIPStarRE/QPBT.lean` import edit at integration time.

### Acceptance criteria

- Every in-scope declaration exists and every definition body is real.
- Edited Lean files type-check; only explicitly tracked Stage 4.2 proof `sorry`s remain.
- Blueprint declarations and direct `\uses` metadata are synchronized faithfully.
- `lake build`, blueprint rendering, declaration checking, and local CI pass on the

After waiting on the fix lock, autofix.sh rechecks only the remote head; a superseded run can leave a newer local commit unpushed, and the waiter then works from the old heads statuses and iteration count. Fail-closed today (evidence re-binds per SHA and the merge gate still requires green on the exact head), so the cost is a wasted fix cycle, not an unsound merge. Recompute local/remote state and the cap under the lock after acquiring it.

body:
<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: gh-common-replace-stale-same-sha-review-bodies -->
Reviewers on the same head SHA can leave a stale review body when a rerun produces a different verdict: gh_common.post_review is marker-idempotent and never replaces an existing review, while post_summary posts the fresh status. The mismatch is fail-closed today (gate 4 needs BOTH the clean body and the green summary), but the stale body is confusing evidence. Port post_review to update (PUT) the existing review body when the marker matches instead of returning exists.
